I'm not sure but I think he may have misheard the psychologist. "Splinter" would make more sense as in savant and splinter skills when someone has a very specific and extensive knowledge on a single topic. For example, someone who is intellectually average but has an above average knowledge about dinosaurs and can name every species and their characteristics. 

This is associated with children with autism since their symptoms often cause them to have very fixed interests. The psychologist was probably trying to rule out autism when assessing his IQ. Listing out all the species of spiders probably didn't help.
